title: 0185-fence-multiple-id-detection-fantasy-sports
universal_lens: The FENCE architecture formalizes Sybil resistance as a dynamic graph partitioning problem. By mapping high-dimensional user attributes to deterministic and probabilistic edges, the system computes connected components under strict O(1) latency constraints, effectively projecting a massive, noisy identity manifold into disjoint equivalence classes for real-time anomaly isolation.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this maps to a conformal inference framework where heuristic equality edges act as hard priors. The cluster scoring function serves as a non-conformity measure; clusters exceeding a 0.95 threshold are flagged as out-of-distribution, triggering Bayesian updates to the underlying user-integrity posterior distributions across the platform.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, FENCE operates as a state-transition filter on the participant layer. It continuously collapses multi-account Sybil states into singular entity nodes, ensuring that downstream predictive models evaluating market liquidity or contest participation operate on a purified, non-redundant state space of independent actors.

reasoning_traces.think:
The FENCE primitive suite derives from the fundamental need to resolve identity ambiguity in high-frequency, adversarial environments. Mathematically, the system constructs a dynamic graph G=(V,E) where V represents user registrations and E is the union of deterministic heuristic edges and probabilistic machine learning edges. The core operator is the connected-component algorithm, which partitions V into disjoint sets C_i. However, standard graph algorithms like Gremlin or the Alternating algorithm scale poorly (O(n) or worse) for real-time inference at 10^8 users. The derived kernel here is the caching-enhanced hybrid: offline batch jobs compute the static component structure, storing mappings in Redis. At runtime, a new node u_new only queries its 1-degree neighbors, inheriting the largest existing cluster ID among them. This reduces the computational complexity from global traversal to O(1) local lookup. The dualities emerge in the scoring phase: cluster size, node type distribution, and n-degree connections are aggregated into a scalar risk score S_c \in [0,1]. This score acts as a decision boundary. If S_c > 0.95, the system executes an automated state transition (blocking). Below this, it triggers a human-in-the-loop feedback loop. Failure modes arise when the heuristic edge generation suffers from high collision rates in shared environments (e.g., NATs), creating false-positive giant components, or when adversaries intentionally fragment their networks to keep S_c below the threshold, exploiting the discrete nature of the actioning boundary.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This lineage traces back to early SybilGuard and SybilLimit protocols in peer-to-peer networks, which utilized random walk distances to bound the influence of malicious nodes. The FENCE architecture modernizes this by replacing theoretical random walks with empirical, high-dimensional attribute matching (IP, device fingerprints) and integrating industrial-grade graph databases (AWS Neptune) and caching layers (Redis) to meet sub-second latency requirements demanded by modern fantasy sports platforms.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The opposing agent is a rational, resource-constrained fraudster aiming to maximize cash-bonus extraction while minimizing detection probability. They model the platform's heuristic rules, anticipating that exact IP matches create edges. Consequently, they employ residential proxy networks or device farms to decouple attributes. The FENCE system counters this by modeling the adversary's coordination cost: even with proxies, subtle correlations in device cleaning patterns or temporal registration bursts create weak edges that the Random Forest link predictor amplifies, eventually collapsing the adversary's fragmented identities into a single high-risk cluster.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition exists between the heuristic edge layer and the ML link prediction layer. If the heuristic layer generates too many false positives due to benign attribute collisions (e.g., university networks), the resulting giant components will saturate the cluster scoring function, rendering the 0.95 threshold meaningless. Furthermore, leakage occurs if the offline reconciliation job lags significantly behind real-time registration spikes, causing the Redis cache to serve stale cluster IDs. The system must enforce a strict anti-collinearity check: if the volume of heuristic edges spikes anomalously without corresponding ML edge validation, the pipeline should temporarily bypass automated blocking to prevent mass false-positive account suspensions.
